name: scRNA-seq Imputation Benchmark Issues
description: On June 25th, 2018, Huang et al. published a computational method SAVER on Nature Methods for imputing dropout gene expression levels in single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. Huang et al. performed a set of comprehensive benchmarking analyses, including comparison with the data from RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization, to demonstrate that SAVER outperformed two existing scRNA-seq imputation methods, scImpute and MAGIC. However, their computational analyses were based on semi-synthetic data that the authors had generated following the Poisson-Gamma model used in the SAVER method. We have therefore re-examined Huang et al.'s study. We find that the semi-synthetic data have very different properties from those of real scRNA-seq data and that the cell clusters used for benchmarking are inconsistent with the cell types labeled by biologists. reputation: A methodological critique paper rather than a standard benchmark, mainly cited in discussions of scRNA-seq imputation evaluation pitfalls.
notes: Not a conventional benchmark dataset; focuses on showing that prior benchmarking was flawed due to semi-synthetic data and inconsistent labels.
